## Summary
- Replace HOME modification with CLAUDE_DIR environment variable for multi-user mode
- Set CLAUDE_DIR to ~/.claude/[username] pattern to give each user their own Claude configuration directory
- Keep HOME unchanged to avoid side effects on other processes

## Changes
- Updated `agentapi_default.sh` to set CLAUDE_DIR instead of HOME for multi-user mode
- Modified `userdir` package to manage CLAUDE_DIR environment variable
- Added new methods `GetUserClaudeDir` and `EnsureUserClaudeDir` for Claude directory management
- Updated tests to verify CLAUDE_DIR behavior

## Benefits
- Cleaner approach that doesn't modify the global HOME environment variable
- Each user gets their own Claude configuration directory at ~/.claude/[username]
- No side effects on other processes that depend on HOME

author: compulim
body:
## Changelog

> Please copy and paste new entries from `CHANGELOG.md` here.

### Added

- Added `withBuildProps` higher-order helper function to extends chain-of-responsibility with props transformation capability, by [@compulim](https://github.com/compulim) in PR [#90](https://github.com/compulim/react-chain-of-responsibility/pull/90)

### Removed

- `createChainOfResponsibilityForFluentUI` is marked as deprecated and will be removed in future releases, by [@compulim](https://github.com/compulim) in PR [#90](https://github.com/compulim/react-chain-of-responsibility/pull/90)
   - Fluent UI v9 no longer use `IRenderFunction` for custom render
   - The correctness of `createChainOfResponsibilityForFluentUI` is no longer validated

## Specific changes

> Please list each individual specific change in this pull request.

- Added `withBuildProps` HOC helper function
   - We tried to add the option to `<Proxy>` and `useBuildComponentCallback`, however, the typing become too complex
   - We tried to add the option to `createChainOfResponsibility`, also too complex
   - We should modify the middleware and run `buildProps` on every middleware so it can support `passModifiedRequest` option
- Deprecated `createChainOfResponsibilityForFluentUI` as it is more difficult to validate `copyRequestToProps` in such scenario
   - We mentioned our plan the deprecate the function in our `README.md`

author: james-garner-canonical
body:
This PR adds the other known interface libraries to the library listing docs. The libraries were found using the methodology described in PR #73 (where only a small number of the known libraries were added initially to simplify review). With the future organisation and review of interface libraries unclear, the status column has only been used to mark deprecated libraries (no recommended libraries yet).

The built page can be seen [here](https://canonical-charmlibs--80.com.readthedocs.build/reference/interface-libs/).

The `generate` extension is updated to wrap interface names in a `no-spellcheck` span even when no url is known for the interface (if a url is known, the link generation code already adds the `no-spellcheck` class). The extension is also updated to filter out unlisted libs for interface libraries (it already does so for non-interface libraries), and handle the 'popular' status.

# Checklist

- [ ] Affected Issues have been mentioned in the Closing issues section
- [ ] Documentation has been written/updated
- [ ] PR title is ready for changelog and subsystem label(s) applied

This refactors the build QoS system to support more builds to run once they have completed the more intensive docker build and push phases of the build process.

This can give the impression of faster builds when there are a lot of builds currently processing. What this allows is for once a build has pushed the images to the registry, it transitions from being a docker build phase to a pre/post rollout phase. This effectively frees up the docker build slot for a new build to come in, up until the total maximum number of builds is reached. What this number is depends on the operator of the cluster and how they determine what they see as an upper limit. A starting point would be double that of the QoS limit, where the default is the same as the QoS limit (effectively no change from current behavior).

Requires changes in https://github.com/uselagoon/build-deploy-tool/pull/390 to properly support this feature (now merged).

author: hamishwillee
body:
Firefox 141 supports `webkitdirectory` on android in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1887878, which was added in #27108

What this does is allow you to mark that an input offers a folder selector, and when you select a folder it returns an array of `File` entries with the path in the [`File.webkitRelativePath`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File/webkitRelativePath) property (see [`HTMLInputElement.webkitdirectory`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement/webkitdirectory#examples) for detail).

But it turns out that on Firefox for Android the returned `webkitRelativePath` is always an empty string.
What I think this means is that FF supports `webkitRelativePath` and `HTMLInputElement/webkitdirectory` in the sense that they exist as entities, but they are both partial implementations.

@danielhjacobs Can you please confirm this.

I have updated the features appropriately.


Related docs work can be tracked in https://github.com/mdn/content/issues/40024

## Summary
- Fixes UX issue where `\!rm` without index provided no user feedback (silent failure)
- Enhanced error handling to provide helpful guidance for missing required arguments
- Improved overall bot error handling framework for better user experience

## Root Cause
When users typed `\!rm` without an index parameter, Discord.py raised `MissingRequiredArgument` but the bot's error handler only logged the error without sending any feedback to users, making the command appear broken.

## Changes Made
### Enhanced Error Handling Framework
- **Upgraded `on_command_error` handler** in `src/main.py` to catch `MissingRequiredArgument`
- **Added specific handling** for `\!rm` command with helpful message
- **Implemented generic fallback** for other commands with missing arguments
- **Maintained existing logging** for debugging purposes

### New Error Message
- **Added `Messages.Command.Remove.MISSING_INDEX`** with clear usage guidance
- **Provides helpful context**: Shows correct syntax + suggests using `\!list` 
- **Consistent with existing patterns**: Follows established message formatting

### Test Coverage
- **Added test** to verify error message exists and is properly formatted
- **Verified integration**: Error handling framework works correctly
- **No regressions**: All existing functionality preserved

## User Experience Improvement
**Before**: Silent failure - no feedback when running `\!rm` without arguments  
**After**: `❌ Please provide an index number. Usage: \!rm <index>`
         `Use \!list to see target indices.`

## Test Results
- ✅ **New test passes**: Error message validation  
- ✅ **14/14 remove command tests pass**: No regressions in existing functionality
- ✅ **3/3 remove integration tests pass**: Full command workflows work correctly
- ✅ **16/16 main module tests pass**: Error handling integration works
- ✅ **All linting passes**: mypy, black, flake8, isort

## Benefits
- **Resolves Issue #67**: Users get clear guidance instead of silent failure
- **Enhanced error framework**: Improved handling for all commands with missing args
- **Better UX**: Helpful error messages with actionable guidance
- **Production ready**: Maintains backward compatibility while improving experience

## Related
- Stacked on #73 (Issue #66 fix) for comprehensive command usability improvements
- Part of critical production issue resolution (#68, #66, #67) before launch
- Establishes pattern for better error handling across all bot commands

body:
This pull request enhances the `src/samples.c` file by introducing support for metadata fields in the `dump_lua` function, adding a new `restore_lua` function for restoring sample data from Lua tables, and refining memory initialization in the `new_lua` function. These changes improve the functionality and robustness of the codebase.

### Enhancements to `dump_lua` function:
* Expanded the table created in `dump_lua` to include 8 fields (4 data arrays and 4 new metadata fields: `capacity`, `count`, `gc_step`, and `base_kb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-13fbd9dc81d9291c0ef7198dff67ba3d681088cf103e251a079fda4fdc376fe7L30-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-13fbd9dc81d9291c0ef7198dff67ba3d681088cf103e251a079fda4fdc376fe7R54-R66)

### New `restore_lua` function:
* Added a new `restore_lua` function to support restoring `measure_samples_t` objects from Lua tables. This function validates metadata fields, ensures array sizes match the metadata, and initializes the `measure_samples_t` object and its data arrays.

### Improvements to `new_lua` function:
* Updated the `new_lua` function to delegate to `restore_lua` when the first argument is a table, enabling restoration mode.
* Corrected the memory initialization for the `data` array to use the size of `measure_samples_data_t` instead of `uint64_t`.

You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project. Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge on their repository to show off their hard work. - [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard) ### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. author: twada
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new "stepwise" assertion format that presents assertion failures as numbered sequential steps, making them more readable and parsable by LLM/AI systems. The implementation spans both the transpiler and runtime components, with significant improvements to multi-line expression handling.

## Motivation

As AI-powered development tools become increasingly prevalent, there's a growing need for assertion libraries to produce output that is easily understood by both humans and language models. Traditional power-assert output, while informative, can be challenging for LLMs to parse effectively.

The stepwise format addresses this by:
- Presenting assertion evaluation as clear, numbered steps
- Grouping related operations by argument
- Providing explicit execution order information
- Making the cause of assertion failures more apparent

## Example Output

```javascript
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]:

# Human-readable format:
assert(scoreOf(rollsOf(frames)) === 132)
       |       |       |        |   |
       |       |       |        |   132
       |       |       |        false
       |       |       [[1,4],[4,5],[6,4],[5,5],[10],[0,1],[7,3],[6,4],[10],[2,8,6]]
       |       [1,4,4,5,6,4,5,5,10,0,1,7,3,6,4,10,2,8,6]
       133

# AI-readable format:
Assertion failed: assert(scoreOf(rollsOf(frames)) === 132)
=== arg:0 ===
Step 1: `frames` => [[1,4],[4,5],[6,4],[5,5],[10],[0,1],[7,3],[6,4],[10],[2,8,6]]
Step 2: `rollsOf(frames)` => [1,4,4,5,6,4,5,5,10,0,1,7,3,6,4,10,2,8,6]
Step 3: `scoreOf(rollsOf(frames))` => 133
Step 4: `132` => 132
Step 5: `scoreOf(rollsOf(frames)) === 132` => false

133 === 132
```

### Single Argument Assertion
```javascript
// Code
const truthy = '1';
const falsy = 0;
assert(truthy === falsy);

// Output

# Human-readable format:
assert(truthy === falsy)
       |      |   |
       |      |   0
       |      false
       "1"

# AI-readable format:
Assertion failed: assert(truthy === falsy)
=== arg:0 ===
Step 1: `truthy` => "1"
Step 2: `falsy` => 0
Step 3: `truthy === falsy` => false

"1" === 0
```

### Multiple Arguments Assertion
```javascript
// Code
const truthy = '1';
const falsy = 0;
assert.equal(truthy, falsy, 'falsy is not truthy');

// Output

# Human-readable format:
assert.equal(truthy, falsy, 'falsy is not truthy')
             |       |      |
             |       |      "falsy is not truthy"
             |       0
             "1"

# AI-readable format:
Assertion failed: assert.equal(truthy, falsy, 'falsy is not truthy')
=== arg:0 ===
Step 1: `truthy` => "1"
=== arg:1 ===
Step 1: `falsy` => 0
=== arg:2 ===
Step 1: `'falsy is not truthy'` => "falsy is not truthy"

"1" === 0
```

## Implementation Overview

The stepwise format implementation spans both transpiler and runtime components. A key architectural improvement is the transition from capturing only `leftIndex` to capturing comprehensive position information through `AssertionRelativeOffset`, enabling accurate expression extraction and better support for multi-line assertions.

### Architecture Design
- **Hybrid approach**: Separates concerns between transpile-time static analysis and runtime dynamic behavior
- **AssertionRelativeOffset**: A key concept introduced in this PR that encapsulates three position values for each captured node:
  - `startPos`: The starting position of the node relative to the assertion statement
  - `endPos`: The ending position of the node relative to the assertion statement
  - `markerPos`: The position where the vertical bar should be displayed in the diagram (formerly `leftIndex`)
  - These offsets are calculated at transpile time using the unified `calculateAssertionRelativeOffsetFor()` API
  - Enables accurate expression extraction even for multi-line assertions
- **argIndex**: Determined at transpile time based on argument position in the assertion call
- **evalOrder**: Captured at runtime based on actual execution order during assertion evaluation
- **Dual output format**: Both human-readable diagram and AI-readable stepwise format are displayed

### Core Components
- **Stepwise Formatter**: New `renderStepwise` function in `packages/runtime/src/stepwise.mts`
- **Runtime Integration**: Modified `runtime.mts` to display both formats on assertion failure
- **Type Refinement**: `AssertionRelativeOffset` for better intention revealing
- **Position Calculation**: Fixed multi-line expression handling with unified API

## Key Changes

### 1. Runtime - Stepwise Formatter (`packages/runtime/src/stepwise.mts`)
```typescript
export function renderStepwise (assertionLine: string, logs: Log[]): string
```
- Groups captured values by `argIndex`
- Sorts steps by `evalOrder` within each argument
- **Expression Extraction**: Uses `startPos` and `endPos` from AssertionRelativeOffset
  - Accurately extracts original expression text using `assertionLine.slice(step.startPos, step.endPos)`
  - Works correctly for both single-line and multi-line expressions
- Formats output as `Step N: 'expression' => value`

### 2. Runtime Integration (`packages/runtime/src/runtime.mts`)
- Modified assertion failure handler to display both formats:
  - Human-readable format: Traditional power-assert diagram
  - AI-readable format: New stepwise output with "Assertion failed:" prefix
- Increments `evalOrder` counter in `ArgumentRecorderImpl` during `tap()` and `rec()` calls
- Captures runtime evaluation order for accurate step sequencing

### 3. Transpiler Core (`packages/transpiler-core`)
- **AssertionRelativeOffset Type**: Renamed from `Address` for intention-revealing naming
  - Defined in `src/address.mts` with three properties: `startPos`, `endPos`, and `markerPos`
  - Provides complete position information for accurate expression extraction
- **Unified Position Calculation**: Introduced `calculateAssertionRelativeOffsetFor()` API
  - Handles both single-line and multi-line assertions correctly
  - Supports different AST node formats (with `range` array or `loc` object or `start`/`end` properties)
  - Calculates proper marker positions for different expression types (member access, operators, etc.)
- **Multi-line Expression Support**: Fixed critical bugs in position calculation
  - Proper handling of line breaks using `columnToPos()` function
  - Accurate offset calculation relative to assertion statement start
  - Ensures expressions spanning multiple lines are extracted correctly
- **Argument Processing**: Enhanced at transpile time
  - `ArgumentModification` class determines `argIndex` for each argument
  - Passes argument indices to runtime via `recorder(argNum)` calls
  - Enables runtime to group captured values by their argument position

### 4. SWC Plugin (`packages/swc-plugin-power-assert`)
- Rust implementation aligned with TypeScript transpiler changes
- Renamed `Utf16NodeAddress` to `AssertionRelativeOffset`
- Consistent metadata structure for cross-transpiler compatibility

### 5. Test Updates
- New unit tests for stepwise formatter in `runtime/src/__tests__/stepwise_test.mts`
- Integration tests updated to verify both output formats
- Multi-line expression test cases added
- All fixture files updated with new metadata structure

## Breaking Changes

None. The stepwise format is an additional output option that doesn't affect existing functionality. The default output format remains unchanged.

## Testing

- ✅ Unit tests for stepwise formatter
- ✅ Integration tests across packages
- ✅ Multi-line expression test cases
- ✅ Updated all fixture files
- ✅ Verified compatibility with existing tools

## Implementation Evolution

The development progressed through several key phases:

1. **Initial Spike Implementation** (commits 05a88cd, 794df93)
   - TypeScript implementation of transpiler-side stepwise reporter
   - Runtime-side stepwise reporter prot

## Summary

Implements a comprehensive maintainer management dashboard for admins to review, override, and manage contributor roles across repositories. This addresses the need for manual maintainer identification and confidence score visibility mentioned in the maintainer evals requirements.

## Key Features

### 🛡️ Maintainer Management Dashboard
- **Role Overview**: View all contributors with their detected roles (owner/maintainer/contributor/bot)
- **Confidence Scores**: Admin-only visibility of algorithm confidence scores (0-100%)
- **Manual Overrides**: Ability to manually change contributor roles with reason tracking
- **Role Locking**: Lock roles to prevent algorithm from changing them during revalidation
- **Comprehensive Filtering**: Filter by repository, role type, confidence level, and detection source

### 🤖 Bot Detection & Management
- **Automatic Bot Detection**: Algorithm detects common bot patterns (`github-actions[bot]`, `dependabot[bot]`, etc.)
- **Bot Role Management**: Separate bot category with dedicated filtering and stats
- **Bot Statistics**: Overview of all automated accounts across repositories

### 📊 Admin Analytics
- **Role Statistics**: Count of owners, maintainers, contributors, and bots
- **Manual Override Tracking**: Number of admin-driven role changes
- **Confidence Distribution**: High confidence role assignments
- **Locked Role Monitoring**: Roles protected from algorithm changes

### 🔒 Security & Audit
- **Admin Authentication**: Restricted to verified admin users only
- **Action Logging**: All role changes logged with admin ID, timestamp, and reason
- **Role History**: Complete audit trail of role changes over time
- **Reason Tracking**: Required explanations for manual overrides

## Implementation Details

### Database Changes
- Added admin override fields to `contributor_roles` table
- Created `override_contributor_role()` function for safe role updates
- Enhanced role constraint to include `'bot'` type
- Added indexes for performance on override and locked role queries

### Frontend Components
- **MaintainerManagement**: Main dashboard component with full CRUD operations
- **Role Change Dialog**: Confirmation modal with reason input and lock option
- **Advanced Filtering**: Repository, role, confidence, and source filters
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly grid layout and responsive tables

### Integration
- Added `/admin/maintainers` route with admin authentication
- Updated admin menu with maintainer management option
- Quick action buttons for common workflows
- Integrated with existing admin auth and logging system

## Usage for Evals

This dashboard provides the foundation for eval-driven algorithm improvements:

1. **Ground Truth Creation**: Admins can manually verify and correct role assignments
2. **Confidence Calibration**: Visibility into algorithm confidence vs actual accuracy
3. **Dataset Generation**: Manual overrides provide high-quality training data
4. **Algorithm Testing**: Compare manual assignments vs algorithmic predictions

## Technical Notes

- Role confidence scores remain private to admin users only
- All database changes use proper RLS policies and admin authentication
- Foreign key constraints ensure data integrity with existing admin users
- Component follows existing admin dashboard patterns (similar to spam management)

body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

A Grafana service that runs on startup, checks for deprecated authentication methods in Prometheus data source configs (sigV4 and Azure auth), installs the relevant data source (Amazon/Azure Prometheus), and migrates the Prometheus data sources to the new Prom DS.

Things worth noting:

- The migration is done by changing the data source type. 
- This does not work for terraform data sources yet. (future PSs)
- Data sources that have been migrated have a flag added to their JSON to help with reverting if needed and debugging.
- Read more about how/why this works in [the design doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vuxqd5JxZefUljeT7_93rFZGreXAWPR6LmxeTsF_tiQ/edit?tab=t.0)

This service is behind a feature flag `prometheusTypeMigration`



**Why do we need this feature?**

We split out AWS and Azure authentication from the [core Prometheus data source](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/prometheus/) and created separate AWS and Azure Prometheus data sources to better support these cloud vendors. Currently, AWS and Azure authentication in the core Prometheus data source is deprecated. [AWS Managed Prometheus](https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/grafana-amazonprometheus-datasource/) and [Azure Monitor Managed Prometheus](https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/grafana-azureprometheus-datasource/) are generally available to customers.

**Who is this feature for?**

Users of Azure/Amazon Prometheus.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes # https://github.com/grafana/data-sources/issues/646

- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.

## Mago 0.26.1

Hello everyone,

This release introduces a new linter rule for best practices and a powerful new formatting option to improve code organization, alongside several key fixes for the formatter.


### ⭐ New Features

- **New Linter Rule: `best-practices/no-sprintf-concatenation`**: A new rule has been added to discourage string concatenation with `sprintf()` calls (e.g., `sprintf(...) . 'string'`). The linter will now suggest incorporating the concatenated parts directly into the `sprintf` format string for better performance and readability. (#139)

- **New Formatter Option: `separate_class_like_members`**: The formatter now inserts a single blank line between different kinds of members inside a class, trait, interface, or enum by default. This visually groups constants, properties, enum cases, trait uses, and methods, making complex class-like structures much easier to read. This behavior can be disabled by setting `separate_class_like_members = false` in your `mago.toml` file. (#223)

### 🛠️ Fixes & Improvements

- **Formatter**: Made several improvements to how member access chains (e.g., `$obj->foo->bar()`) are formatted for better consistency and readability. (#218, #205)
- **Formatter**: Fixed a bug where match expressions used within a string concatenation (.) were not formatted correctly. (#207)

Thank you for your contributions and for helping us improve Mago!

body:
This pull request introduces several key updates to the EcoDex app, including enhancements to onboarding, species identification, and API integrations. The changes streamline user experience for new users, improve species data retrieval, and refactor the codebase for better maintainability.

### Onboarding Enhancements
* Added onboarding flow for new users, including a `setupProfile` screen where users can set a username. This is managed using the `isNewUser` flag in the authentication context.

### Species Identification Improvements
* Replaced hardcoded AI summary generation with reusable hooks (`fetchSpeciesName` and `fetchSpeciesSummary`) for species name and metadata retrieval using the Gemini API.

### API Key and Configuration Updates
* Added support for `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` in `app.config.js` to allow for EAS build configurations to identify keys

### UI and Feature Enhancements
* Introduced an `InfoBox` component to display species metadata (e.g., height, weight, lifespan) on the entry submission screen. Added a visual rarity indicator using a gradient color scheme.
* Updated the `README.md` to reflect the new APK download link for Android users and added Gemini API details under the "Identifying Entries" section.

### Code Cleanup and Refactoring
* Removed legacy AI summary generation logic and unused constants related to the HuggingFace API, simplifying the `submitEntry` component.

### Testing
* Implemented Vitest unit testing, with basic tests set up for key hooks.

This PR implements a complete test infrastructure for the scripts repository and extracts common functionality into reusable modules, significantly improving development efficiency and code maintainability.

## 🧪 Test Infrastructure

Added comprehensive testing with **51 tests** and **143 assertions**, all passing:

- **Test Structure**: Created `test/` directory with `unit/` and `integration/` subdirectories
- **Test Helper**: Added `test/test_helper.rb` with common testing utilities
- **Rake Tasks**: Added `Rakefile` with organized test execution (`rake test`, `rake unit`, `rake integration`)
- **Test Coverage**: 6 unit test files + 5 integration test files covering all shared modules and key scripts

## 📚 Shared Libraries

Extracted common functionality into 7 reusable modules in `lib/`:

- **ErrorHandling**: Consistent error handling with `error_exit`
- **DependencyChecker**: Command dependency validation with `check_dependency`  
- **LlmUtils**: LLM model flag handling and execution utilities
- **ClipboardUtils**: Cross-platform clipboard functionality
- **ShellUtils**: Safe shell command execution with error handling
- **MeetingFileUtils**: Meeting-specific file operations and utilities
- **LlmWorkflowUtils**: Complex LLM workflow operations

## 🔧 Script Refactoring

Updated existing scripts to use shared modules:

```ruby
# Before: Duplicated error handling in every script
def error_exit(message)
  puts "Error: #{message}"
  exit 1
end

# After: Import and use shared module
require 'error_handling'
include ErrorHandling
# Now can use error_exit() from shared module
```

body:
This PR implements support for custom email addresses in push notifications, allowing users to specify their own email address for the VAPID_SUBJECT field instead of using a hardcoded default.

## Changes Made

### Manager API (`/api/send-notification`)
- Added optional `email` parameter to the request payload
- Implemented email validation using regex pattern `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/`
- Updated VAPID_SUBJECT to use `mailto:{email}` format when custom email is provided
- Maintains backward compatibility - falls back to environment variable or default email when no custom email is provided
- Returns HTTP 400 error for invalid email formats

### Register Handler (`handler.py`)
- Modified `send_push_notification()` function to accept optional `email` parameter
- Updated function call to pass user's email address to the Manager API
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing function signature

## API Usage Examples

**With custom email:**
```json
{
  "message": "Registration completed!",
  "subscription": { ... },
  "email": "user@example.com"
}
```

**Without email (backward compatible):**
```json
{
  "message": "Registration completed!",
  "subscription": { ... }
}
```

## Testing

- ✅ Email validation accepts valid email addresses
- ✅ Email validation rejects invalid formats
- ✅ Backward compatibility maintained
- ✅ Proper error handling for missing subscriptions
- ✅ Build process succeeds
- ✅ Added comprehensive test file (`manager/test-notification.rest`)

## Technical Details

The implementation uses minimal, surgical changes to maintain existing functionality while adding the new email feature. The email validation is intentionally simple but effective, and the VAPID_SUBJECT formatting follows the standard `mailto:` protocol scheme.

Fixes #58.

body:
Fixes #14107

### Summary

This PR fixes an issue where `SparsePauliOp.is_unitary()` was not properly respecting the input tolerance values when checking if an operator is unitary. The method was not passing the tolerance parameters to the internal [simplify()] call.

### Details and comments

The main changes in this PR are:

1. Modified `SparsePauliOp.is_unitary()` to pass the atol and rtol parameters to the [simplify()] method
2. Added a test case that verifies the fix works as expected by:
   - Creating a matrix that's approximately unitary but not exactly
   - Verifying it's considered unitary with appropriate tolerances
   - Verifying it's not considered unitary with very tight tolerances

### Testing
- [x] I have added the tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] I have read the CONTRIBUTING document.

### Release Notes

Fixed an issue where `SparsePauliOp.is_unitary()` was not respecting the input tolerance values when checking if an operator is unitary.

author: imanadi
body:
### Overview
This PR establishes the foundational MVP implementation for Grayskull, a secret management service. It introduces a modular, extensible architecture with Spring Boot-based REST APIs, persistence-agnostic SPI interfaces, MongoDB-backed storage, fine-grained authorization, comprehensive auditing, and containerized local development setup.

---

### REST API Layer (`SecretController`)

**Endpoints:**
```
GET    /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets
       - List secrets with pagination (offset/limit)
       - Secured: secrets.list permission
       - Returns latest version of each secret

POST   /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets
       - Create new secret with initial data (version 1)
       - Secured: secrets.create permission
       - Supports SELF provider with public/private parts

GET    /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets/{secretName}
       - Read secret metadata (name, version, timestamps, state)
       - Secured: secrets.read.metadata permission
       - Excludes sensitive data values

GET    /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets/{secretName}/data
       - Read decrypted secret value
       - Secured: secrets.read.value permission
       - Returns both public and private parts

POST   /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets/{secretName}/data
       - Upgrade secret data (creates new version)
       - Secured: secrets.update permission
       - Immutable versioning: previous versions preserved

DELETE /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets/{secretName}
       - Soft-delete (marks as DISABLED)
       - Secured: secrets.delete permission
       - Audit trail maintained

GET    /v1/projects/{projectId}/secrets/{secretName}/versions/{version}
       - Admin API: Retrieve specific version
       - Secured: secrets.read.version permission
       - Supports state filtering (ACTIVE/DISABLED/DELETED)
```

**Request/Response Handling:**
- Jakarta Bean Validation for input sanitization (`@Valid`, `@NotBlank`, `@Size`, constraint ranges)
- `ResponseTemplate<T>` wrapper with success/error indicators and messages

---

### Architecture & Module Structure

#### 1. SPI Module (Service Provider Interface)
**Purpose:** Defines persistence-agnostic contracts and domain models for extensibility.

**Key Components:**
- **Interfaces:**
  - `GrayskullAuthorizationProvider`: Pluggable authorization provider SPI
  - `SecretRepository`, `SecretDataRepository`, `ProjectRepository`, `AuditEntryRepository`: Persistence-agnostic repository contracts
  
- **Domain Models:** `Secret`, `SecretData`, `Project`, `AuditEntry` with lifecycle states (`ACTIVE`, `DISABLED`, `DELETED`)

- **Authorization Context:** `AuthorizationContext` for project and secret-level permission checks

**Design Philosophy:** Zero external dependencies (only provided-scope framework deps), enabling future implementations (e.g., different databases, cloud provider integrations)

#### 2. Server Module
**Core Spring Boot application providing business logic and persistence.**

##### Authorization Framework
**Implementation:**
- **`GrayskullSecurity`**: Security facade bean for `@PreAuthorize` expressions
  - `hasPermission(projectId, action)` - Project-level checks (e.g., create, list)
  - `hasPermission(projectId, secretName, action)` - Secret-level checks (e.g., read, update)
  
- **`SimpleAuthorizationProvider`**: Configuration-driven rule engine with wildcard support
  - Rules defined in `application.yml` under `grayskull.authorization.rules`
  - Supports user, project, and secret-level matching with `*` wildcards
  
- **`AuthorizationProperties`**: Type-safe configuration binding for authorization rules

**Action Definitions (`GrayskullActions`):** 
- `secrets.create`, `secrets.list`, `secrets.read.metadata`, `secrets.read.value`, `secrets.read.version`, `secrets.update`, `secrets.delete`

**Authorization Logic:**
- Non-existent projects → Transient project with default KMS key for create operations
- Non-existent secrets → Fallback to project-level rules (allows permission checks before resource exists)
- Existing resources → Full secret-level permission evaluation

##### Audit Framework (AOP-based)
**Implementation:**
- **`@Audit`** annotation with `AuditAction` enum for marking auditable operations
- **`AuditAspect`**: Spring AOP aspect with `@AfterReturning` advice
  
**Behavior:**
- Audits only successful CUD (Create, Update, Delete) operations
- Captures: `userId`, `projectId`, `resourceType`, `resourceName`, `resourceVersion`, `action`, `timestamp`
- Metadata includes sanitized request/response payloads
- **Masking:** `@AuditMask` annotation + custom Jackson serializer for PII/sensitive data
- Transaction-aligned: Failures in audit serialization rollback the entire operation

##### Service Layer
**`SecretService` / `SecretServiceImpl`:**
- Secret lifecycle management with versioning (immutable secret data)
- Soft-delete implementation (marks secrets as `DISABLED`)
- KMS key inheritance from project configuration
- Concurrency: Optimistic locking via MongoDB version field

##### Exception Handling
**`GlobalExceptionHandler`** (`@RestControllerAdvice`):
- Centralized exception handling with consistent error responses
- Validation errors return detailed `Violation` objects
- Custom exceptions mapped to appropriate HTTP status codes

##### Persistence Layer
**MongoDB Implementation:**
- Entity classes: `SecretEntity`, `SecretDataEntity`, `ProjectEntity`, `AuditEntryEntity`
- Repository implementations: Delegates to `MongoRepository` interfaces
- Timestamp generation delegated to DB (`@CreatedDate`, `@LastModifiedDate`)
- Separate collections for metadata and data (optimized reads)

##### Configuration
- **`CryptoConfig`**: Manages encryption keys (bound to `grayskull.crypto.keys.*`)
- **`KmsConfig`**: Default KMS key configuration
- **`SecurityConfiguration`**: Spring Security with Basic Auth
- **`MongoBeanConfiguration`**: Auditing enablement, custom converters

#### 3. Setup Module
**Local Development Environment:**
- Docker Compose setup for 3-node MongoDB replica set (ports 37017-37019)
- Authentication with keyfile-based security
- Scripts: `setup.sh` (automated initialization), `teardown.sh` (cleanup)
- Environment configuration via `.env` file

#### 4. Simple-App Module
**Purpose:** Example application demonstrating Grayskull integration as a library.

---

### Testing Strategy

**Framework:** JUnit 5 + Spring Boot Test + Testcontainers

**`BaseIntegrationTest`:**
- Spins up ephemeral MongoDB container per test run
- `@DynamicPropertySource` for runtime configuration
- Provides helper methods for API operations with user context
- 12 test classes covering controllers, mappers, models, and authorization

**Test Coverage:**
- **API Tests:** `SecretControllerIT` - CRUD operations, pagination, versioning, authorization scenarios
- **Unit Tests:** `SecretMapperTest`, `SecretTest`, `SecretDataTest`, `AuditMaskingSerializerTest`
- **Authorization Tests:** Multi-role scenarios (admin, editor, viewer) with `@PreAuthorize` validation

**Test Configuration (`test/resources/application.yml`):**
- Predefined authorization rules for consistent test behavior
- User roles: `admin` (full access), `editor` (create/read/update), `viewer` (read-only)

---

### Build & Tooling

**Maven Multi-Module:**
- Parent POM with centralized dependency management
- Spring Boot 3.5.0, Java 21
- Dependencies: Spring Data MongoDB, Spring Security, MapStruct, Lombok, Jackson, Testcontainers

# プルリクエスト: レスポンシブデザイン実装

## 概要
「ちいくさ日記」アプリケーションに対して、モバイル端末での使いやすさを向上させるため、全画面にわたってレスポンシブデザインを実装しました。PCとモバイルの両方で最適な表示・操作性を実現しています。

## 実装内容

### 1. ナビゲーション改善
- **PCサイドバーナビゲーション**: 左側に固定表示される専用ナビゲーションを実装
- **モバイルボトムナビゲーション**: 画面下部に固定される親指操作しやすいナビゲーションを実装
- **バックボタンの廃止**: 全画面から戻るボタンを削除し、ナビゲーションの一貫性を向上

### 2. レスポンシブレイアウト実装
- **日記関連画面**: 新規作成・編集・詳細・一覧画面のレスポンシブ対応
- **統計画面**: グラフのサイズ調整と配置の最適化
- **プロフィール・設定画面**: モバイルでの表示改善
- **ホーム画面**: ロゴとボタン配置の調整

### 3. カレンダー表示改善
- モバイルでのカレンダー表示を最適化（セルサイズ・フォントサイズ調整）
- 横スクロール対応でカレンダーの表示崩れを防止
- タッチ操作しやすいボタンサイズに調整

### 4. UI/UX改善
- モバイルでのタッチターゲットサイズを適切に調整（最小44px）
- フォントサイズ・パディング・マージンをデバイスサイズに応じて最適化
- 水やり機能をナビゲーションに統合し、アクセシビリティ向上
- タネカウンターの表示位置を各画面で統一

### 5. 技術的改善
- Tailwind CSSのレスポンシブユーティリティクラスを活用
- Stimulusコントローラーの不要な干渉を削除
- PWAマニフェストエンドポイントの追加準備

## 変更ファイル
- 27ファイルに及ぶ広範な変更（+632行、-668行）
- 主な変更対象：
  - ビューファイル（`.html.erb`）
  - CSSファイル（`application.tailwind.css`）
  - JavaScriptコントローラー
  - ルーティング設定

## テスト確認事項
- [x] PCブラウザでの表示・動作確認
- [x] モバイルサイズでの表示・動作確認（デベロッパーツール）
- [x] ナビゲーションの動作確認
- [x] フォーム入力の動作確認
- [x] カレンダー表示の確認
- [x] 既存のテストケースのパス確認

## 今後の展望
このレスポンシブデザイン実装により、ユーザーがどこからでも快適に日記を記録できるようになりました。特にモバイルユーザーの利便性が大幅に向上し、毎日の継続的な記録がより簡単になります。

body: I hereby agree to the terms of the CLA available at: https://docs.databend.com/dev/policies/cla/ ## Summary ##### feat(meta): Add conflict-free sequence generator v1 Introduce a new conflict-free sequence generator (storage version 1) alongside the existing version 0 generator. The v1 generator eliminates conflicts during concurrent sequence number generation by using a new `FetchAddU64` operation instead of check-and-set semantics. Key changes: - V1 generator stores sequence values in external standalone keys - Uses atomic FetchAddU64 operation for conflict-free updates - V0 generator remains unchanged for backward compatibility The FetchAddU64 operation performs in-place atomic updates without requiring metadata assertions, eliminating conflicts between concurrent sequence requests and improving throughput for sequence generation workloads. Both storage versions coexist, allowing gradual migration from the conflict-prone v0 implementation to the high-concurrency v1 design. **Non-Breaking**: This Commit just add this function but does not used anywhere. ## Tests - [x] Unit Test - [ ] Logic Test - [ ] Benchmark Test - [ ] No Test - _Explain why_ ## Type of change - [x] Other ## Related Issues - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/databendlabs/databend/18273)

author: copilot
body:
This PR significantly enhances the `Interval` class to improve its robustness, readability, and mathematical correctness. The changes address verbose methods, add comprehensive testing, and implement proper exception handling as requested in the issue.

## Key Improvements

### 🐛 **Critical Bug Fixes**
- **Fixed NPE in `isEmpty()` method**: The method was calling `.equals()` on potentially null `minimum` field, causing crashes when working with empty intervals
- **Fixed potential NPE in `isDegenerate()` method**: Added null checks before calling `.equals()`

### 🏗️ **Refactored Verbose Methods**
- **`mergeWith()`**: Replaced repetitive if-else logic with clean helper methods:
  - `selectMinimum()` and `selectMaximum()` for boundary selection
  - `shouldIncludeMinimum()` and `shouldIncludeMaximum()` for inclusion logic
- **`isProperSupersetOf()`**: Eliminated the complex 40+ line method with systematic approach:
  - `containsInterval()`, `isMinimumContained()`, `isMaximumContained()` helpers
  - Removed the "algorithm could be improved" TODO comment
- **`overlapsWith()`**: Replaced the commented "more elegant implementation needed" with mathematically sound algorithm using `isBeforeInterval()` helper

### ⚠️ **Enhanced Exception Handling**
- **Created custom exception hierarchy**:
  - `IntervalException` (base class)
  - `InvalidIntervalOperationException` (for operation failures like merging non-overlapping intervals)
  - `InvalidIntervalException` (for invalid interval construction)
- **Replaced generic exceptions** with descriptive custom exceptions containing contextual error messages

### 📚 **Comprehensive Documentation**
- **Enhanced class-level JavaDoc** with mathematical background and Allen's interval algebra references
- **Added detailed method documentation** with algorithm explanations, complexity notes, and parameter descriptions
- **Documented thread safety guarantees** (class is immutable)

### 🧪 **Extensive Test Coverage**
Added 21 comprehensive unit tests covering:
- **Edge cases**: Empty intervals, degenerate intervals, boundary conditions
- **Allen's interval algebra**: All 13 possible interval relationships validated
- **Boundary inclusion logic**: Mixed open/closed interval operations
- **Exception scenarios**: Invalid construction and operation attempts
- **Mathematical correctness**: Subset/superset relationships, containment, overlap detection

## Example Usage

```java
// Before: Risk of NPE and unclear error messages
Interval<Integer> empty = Interval.getEmptyInterval();
empty.isEmpty(); // ❌ NullPointerException

Interval<Integer> a = Interval.makeClosedInterval(1, 3);
Interval<Integer> b = Interval.makeClosedInterval(5, 7);
a.mergeWith(b); // ❌ Generic UnsupportedOperationException

// After: Robust with clear error messages
empty.isEmpty(); // ✅ Returns true safely

try {
    a.mergeWith(b);
} catch (InvalidIntervalOperationException e) {
    // ✅ Clear message: "Cannot merge non-overlapping intervals: [1,3] and [5,7]"
}
```

## Mathematical Correctness

The implementation now properly handles all cases from Allen's interval algebra:
- **Before**: Relations like `[1,3)` and `[3,5]` had inconsistent overlap detection
- **After**: Correctly identifies they overlap at point 3, following mathematical interval theory

## Breaking Changes

⚠️ **Exception Types**: Code catching `UnsupportedOperationException` from `mergeWith()` should now catch `InvalidIntervalOperationException`

## Testing

All existing tests continue to pass, plus 21 new tests ensure comprehensive coverage:
```bash
mvn test  # ✅ All tests pass
```

The changes maintain backward compatibility while significantly improving the class's robustness and usability.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a simplified "log trace" feature that helps users debug their configuration by showing the chain of successful matches in a concise, single-line format.

## Problem

The existing `tracing` crate provides detailed debugging information for implementation details, but it's too verbose for users who just want to understand why a certain input got mapped to a particular output URL. Users need a concise way to see the matching chain without all the internal logging noise.

## Solution

Added a structured `LogTrace` data type that tracks the chain of successful matches and displays them in the format:

```
OK: input-1 + regex(pattern-1) => input-2 + prefix(prefix-1) => input-3 + fuzzy(fuzzy-1) => url
```

### Examples

**Simple match:**
```
OK: Hello + exact(Hello) => https://example.com?q=Hello
```

**Chained match:**
```
OK: animals/dag + regex(^animals/(.*)) => dag + fuzzy(dog) => https://animals.com/dag
```

## Key Features

- **Structured data**: Built as a data structure internally, not string-based
- **Only successful paths**: Shows only the chain that led to a successful match, not failed attempts
- **Always visible**: Logged at info level by default, even without `--info` flag
- **Clean separation**: Log trace goes to stderr, URL output goes to stdout
- **Backward compatible**: All existing functionality preserved

## Implementation Details

1. **New data structures**: Added `LogTrace` and `TraceStep` to track matching chains
2. **Updated trait**: Modified `Matcher` trait to return `(String, LogTrace)` instead of just `String`
3. **All matchers updated**: Updated exact, prefix, fuzzy, regex, and list matchers to build traces
4. **Smart logging**: Uses tracing when info level is enabled, falls back to stderr otherwise
5. **Comprehensive tests**: Added tests for simple matches, chained matches, and no-match scenarios

Fixes #19.

  * 미션 상세, 피드백 제출, 미션 과제 목록 등 미션 관련 상세 페이지 및 컴포넌트가 추가되었습니다.
  * 배움일기(스터디 다이어리) 목록, 작성, 상세, 편집, 나의 활동 등 일기 기능이 새롭게 도입되었습니다.
  * 칭찬(프레이즈) 목록, 인기 칭찬, 상세 모달, 이모지 반응, 댓글 등 칭찬 기능이 대폭 확장되었습니다.
  * 상점(Shop) 상품 구매, 구매 내역, 어드민 상품 등록/삭제 등 상점 기능이 개선 및 스타일링되었습니다.
  * 브레드크럼(경로 표시) 기능이 전역적으로 추가되어 페이지 이동 시 현재 위치를 쉽게 파악할 수 있습니다.
  * 날짜 범위 선택, 달력 등 다양한 커스텀 UI 컴포넌트가 추가되었습니다.

* **버그 수정**
  * 일부 이미지 경로, URL, import 경로 등에서 대소문자 오류 및 하드코딩된 URL이 동적으로 개선되었습니다.

* **스타일**
  * 미션, 칭찬, 상점, 배움일기 등 주요 페이지와 컴포넌트에 SCSS/CSS 모듈 기반의 새로운 디자인이 적용되었습니다.
  * 반응형 레이아웃, 버튼, 입력폼, 카드 등 UI 요소의 시각적 일관성과 접근성이 향상되었습니다.

* **리팩터링**
  * axios 인스턴스 및 API 요청 방식이 중앙 집중화되어 코드 일관성과 유지보수성이 높아졌습니다.
  * 인라인 스타일이 CSS/SCSS 모듈로 대체되었습니다.
  * 상태 관리 및 데이터 흐름이 개선되었습니다.

* **문서화**
  * 각 컴포넌트 및 서비스 함수에 대한 설명과 내역이 코드 주석 및 구조로 보강되었습니다.

* **기타 작업**
  * 여러 신규 의존성(`date-fns`, `react-datepicker`)이 추가되었습니다.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

✅ **Please merge!**

I'll automatically update this PR to resolve conflicts as long as you don't change it yourself.

If you'd like to skip this version, you can just close this PR. If you have any feedback, just mention me in the comments below.

Configure Scala Steward for your repository with a [`.scala-steward.conf`](https://github.com/scala-steward-org/scala-steward/blob/31f8cb648396db258f0ae31b31be0fef04a641dc/docs/repo-specific-configuration.md) file.

_Have a fantastic day writing Scala!_

<details>
<summary>⚙ Adjust future updates</summary>

Add this to your `.scala-steward.conf` file to ignore future updates of this dependency:
```
updates.ignore = [ { groupId = "org.scalameta", artifactId = "sbt-scalafmt" } ]
```
Or, add this to slow down future updates of this dependency:
```
dependencyOverrides = [{
  pullRequests = { frequency = "30 days" },
  dependency = { groupId = "org.scalameta", artifactId = "sbt-scalafmt" }
}]
```

author: enreign
body:
## Summary

This PR implements an enhanced version of the Freshdesk MCP server with advanced features inspired by the Productboard MCP implementation. The enhanced server runs alongside the original server for backward compatibility.

## Key Features

### 🔐 Permission System
- Automatic API endpoint testing to discover user permissions
- Permission-based tool registration - only accessible tools are registered
- Comprehensive permission types for all Freshdesk resources
- Access level hierarchy (READ, WRITE, DELETE, ADMIN)

### 🏗️ Enhanced Architecture
- Modular resource APIs with dedicated classes for each resource type
- Tool registry system for dynamic tool management
- Enhanced base tool class with permission metadata support
- Improved error handling with custom error types

### 🔍 Tool Discovery
- New `discovery` tool that provides:
  - List of available tools based on permissions
  - Current user permissions and capabilities
  - Detailed capability information
- Dynamic tool information instead of static definitions

### 📊 Health Monitoring & Metrics
- Health endpoint with API, auth, and rate limit checks
- Metrics collection (request counts, response times, uptime)
- Production-ready monitoring capabilities

### 🛠️ Enhanced Tools
All tools reimplemented with:
- Comprehensive parameter validation using Zod
- Permission metadata for access control
- Consistent response formatting
- Better error handling

## Usage

```bash
# Development
npm run dev:enhanced

# Production
npm run build
npm run start:enhanced

# Using launch script
./scripts/launch-enhanced.sh
```

## Testing

```bash
npm test tests/enhanced-server.test.ts
```

## Documentation

See [ENHANCED_SERVER.md](ENHANCED_SERVER.md) for detailed documentation.

## Backward Compatibility

The enhanced server runs independently of the original server:
- Original: `npm start` or `node dist/index.js`
- Enhanced: `npm run start:enhanced` or `node dist/index-enhanced.js`

This allows for gradual migration and testing.

author: rsimon
body:
## In this PR

The [upgrade from OpenSeadragon 4 to 5](https://github.com/recogito/recogito-client/commit/64778320ca3a75a2ddc195839786d7e3ac8f2c46) introduced a regression for self-hosted setups: self-hosted setups require that OSD sends the auth token in the `Authorization` header along with requests to `info.json` as well as image tiles. However, this no longer worked in OSD 5.

This PR changes the OSD config to the pattern recommended in [this OSD issue](https://github.com/openseadragon/openseadragon/issues/2659).

body: ### Description # Add Asset Detail Page for Wallet Tokens ## Overview This PR introduces a new asset detail page that provides comprehensive information about wallet tokens, accessible via `/wallet/:slug` routes. The page offers a unified view of token balances, insights, and transaction history. ## Key Changes ### New Asset Detail Page Structure - **`AssetDetailPage.tsx`**: Main page component with routing validation and header setup - **`AssetDetailTabs.tsx`**: Tab navigation between Home, Perks, and Transactions views - **`AssetDetailContent.tsx`**: Main content layout with balance and info sections ### Core Components - **`BalanceSection.tsx`**: Interactive balance display with buy/sell/send/receive actions - Zero balance state with "Buy" and "Receive" buttons - Has balance state with full action suite and dollar value display - Mobile-responsive transfer drawer integration - **`AssetInfoSection.tsx`**: Token information with banner, description, and CTA - **`AssetInsights.tsx`**: Metrics dashboard showing price, holders, volume, and transfers ### Routing Updates - Added `ASSET_DETAIL_PAGE` route (`/wallet/:slug`) - Updated `WebPlayer.jsx` to handle new asset detail routing - Maintains backward compatibility with existing wallet routes ### UI/UX Enhancements - **Wallet Messages**: Added `buy`, `send`, and `receive` action labels - **Responsive Design**: Desktop-optimized layout with defined section widths - **Visual Polish**: Cover photo backgrounds, token icons, and user badges integration ### How Has This Been Tested? `npm run web:prod` and go to `/wallet/audio`

author: metanull
body:
# Pull Request: Implement Contextualization Feature

## Overview
This PR implements a comprehensive `Contextualization` feature that allows storing contextualized information for both Items and Details in the museum inventory application.

## Changes Made

### Database Schema
- **New Migration**: `create_contextualizations_table.php`
  - UUID primary key with auto-generation
  - Foreign keys to `contexts`, `items`, and `details` tables
  - Constraint ensuring exactly one of `item_id` or `detail_id` is set
  - JSON `extra` field for extensible data storage
  - Standard `internal_name` and `backward_compatibility` fields

### Models & Business Logic
- **New Model**: `Contextualization` with proper relationships and scopes
- **Enhanced Models**: Added `contextualizations()` relationship to `Item`, `Detail`, and `Context` models
- **Special Methods**: `createWithDefaultContext()` for simplified default context operations
- **Scopes**: `default()`, `forContext()`, `forItems()`, `forDetails()` for filtered queries
- **Proper Context Integration**: Uses Context model scopes instead of manual where clauses

### API Layer
- **New Resource**: `ContextualizationResource` for consistent API responses
- **New Controller**: `ContextualizationController` with full CRUD operations
- **Additional Endpoints**:
  - `GET /contextualizations/default-context` - List contextualizations from default context
  - `GET /contextualizations/for-items` - List contextualizations for items only
  - `GET /contextualizations/for-details` - List contextualizations for details only
  - `POST /contextualizations/default-context` - Create with default context
- **Validation**: Comprehensive request validation ensuring data integrity

### Factory & Seeding
- **New Factory**: `ContextualizationFactory` with state methods for different scenarios
- **New Seeder**: `ContextualizationSeeder` for sample data generation
- **Enhanced Detail Factory**: Fixed to always create with associated Item

### Testing
- **Unit Tests**: `FactoryTest` covering all factory scenarios
- **Feature Tests**: Complete test suite covering:
  - `AnonymousTest` - Authorization testing
  - `IndexTest` - Listing and pagination
  - `ShowTest` - Individual resource retrieval
  - `StoreTest` - Resource creation with validation
  - `UpdateTest` - Resource modification with constraint validation
  - `DestroyTest` - Resource deletion

## Key Features
1. **Flexible Association**: Each contextualization belongs to either an Item OR a Detail
2. **Context Integration**: Full integration with existing Context system using proper scopes
3. **Default Context Support**: Simplified operations for default context
4. **Extensible Design**: JSON field for future data requirements
5. **Comprehensive Validation**: Ensures data integrity at application level
6. **Full Test Coverage**: 61 tests covering all scenarios

## Validation Rules
- Exactly one of `item_id` or `detail_id` must be provided
- `context_id` is required and must exist
- `internal_name` is required and unique
- Foreign key constraints ensure referential integrity

## API Examples
```php
// Create contextualization for an item
POST /contextualizations
{
    "context_id": "uuid",
    "item_id": "uuid",
    "internal_name": "unique-name",
    "extra": {"key": "value"}
}

// Create with default context
POST /contextualizations/default-context
{
    "detail_id": "uuid", 
    "internal_name": "unique-name"
}

// List contextualizations for items only
GET /contextualizations/for-items

// List contextualizations from default context
GET /contextualizations/default-context
```

## Code Quality Improvements
- **Proper Scope Usage**: Uses `Context::default()` scope instead of manual `where('is_default', true)` clauses
- **Consistent Patterns**: Follows established Laravel and project conventions
- **Maintainable Code**: Leverages existing model methods for better abstraction

## Testing Results
- ✅ All 637 tests pass (including 61 new contextualization tests)
- ✅ PHPStan/Pint code quality checks pass
- ✅ 100% test coverage for new functionality

## Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE contextualizations (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    context_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES contexts(id),
    item_id UUID NULL REFERENCES items(id),
    detail_id UUID NULL REFERENCES details(id),
    extra JSON NULL,
    internal_name VARCHAR UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    backward_compatibility VARCHAR NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP,
    -- Constraint: exactly one of item_id or detail_id must be set
);
```

This implementation follows the established patterns in the codebase and maintains backward compatibility while adding powerful new contextualization capabilities for the museum inventory system.

This PR implements a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Formanator, enabling AI assistants and other MCP clients to interact with Forma accounts programmatically.

The server provides three essential tools as requested:

1. **`listBenefitsWithCategories`** - Lists all available Forma benefits with their categories and remaining balances

- Reuses existing `.formanatorrc.json` configuration file for authentication

- Leverages existing API functions from `forma.ts` for all operations

```bash
# Start the MCP server (requires authentication)
formanator mcp
```

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The application was failing to deploy on Railway because the `prisma` directory was missing at runtime. This caused Prisma Client to be unable to find the schema file, preventing the application from connecting to the database.

The deployment would fail with errors like:
```
Error: Could not load --schema from provided path prisma/schema.prisma: file or directory not found
```

## Root Cause

While the Dockerfile was copying the entire `./server` directory in the backend build stage, the Prisma directory wasn't being explicitly copied in the base build stages that set up the container environment. This meant that when the docker-entrypoint.sh script tried to run Prisma commands with explicit schema paths:

```bash
npx prisma generate --schema=/app/server/prisma/schema.prisma
npx prisma migrate deploy --schema=/app/server/prisma/schema.prisma
```

The `/app/server/prisma` directory didn't exist, causing the deployment to fail.

## Solution

Added explicit `COPY` instructions for the `server/prisma` directory to both architecture-specific build stages (ARM64 and AMD64):

```dockerfile
COPY --chown=anythingllm:anythingllm ./server/prisma /app/server/prisma
```

This ensures that:
- The Prisma directory is available early in the build process
- The directory structure matches what the entrypoint script expects
- Proper ownership is maintained with the `anythingllm` user
- Both ARM64 and AMD64 architectures are supported

## Testing

- ✅ Validated Dockerfile syntax with hadolint
- ✅ Successfully built Docker base stage to verify syntax correctness
- ✅ Confirmed the `server/prisma` directory exists in the source with required files:
  - `schema.prisma`
  - `seed.js` 
  - `migrations/` directory

## Impact

This change is minimal and surgical - it only adds the missing Prisma directory copy without modifying any existing functionality. The fix ensures Railway deployments will have access to the Prisma schema at runtime, allowing the application to successfully connect to the database.

Fixes deployment issues on Railway and potentially other container platforms that may have similar file availability constraints.

- Implemented a conditional check to verify the `String` is not `null` before accessing its length.
- If the `String` is `null`, the method now handles this case appropriately, preventing the exception.
- Reviewed the logic leading to this method to ensure the variable is either initialized or handled safely.

## Impact

- **Prevents application crashes** due to unhandled `NullPointerException` in this method.
- **Improves user experience** by ensuring the app remains stable during button interactions.
- **Enhances code robustness** by guarding against potential null values.

author: christolis
body:
Throughout this entire time, for anybody cloning the repository, setting up the `config.json.template`, following all the steps from the GitHub wiki we have verbatim and running the bot, leads to a SLF4J(E) stacktrace into the console almost as soon as the program begins execution, regardless of the environment:

    SLF4J(E): Unexpected problem occurred during version sanity check
    SLF4J(E): Reported exception:
    java.lang.AbstractMethodError: Receiver class org.apache.logging.slf4j.SLF4JServiceProvider does not define or inherit an implementation of the resolved method 'abstract java.lang.String getRequestedApiVersion()' of interface org.slf4j.spi.SLF4JServiceProvider.
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.versionSanityCheck(LoggerFactory.java:385)
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.performInitialization(LoggerFactory.java:189)
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getProvider(LoggerFactory.java:511)
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getILoggerFactory(LoggerFactory.java:497)
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getLogger(LoggerFactory.java:446)
	at org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getLogger(LoggerFactory.java:472)
	at org.togetherjava.tjbot.Application.<clinit>(Application.java:35)

There has been no major hurdle noted after this exception being thrown, at least not one that I am personally aware of.

Fix this by updating `log4j-slf4j2-impl` to the latest stable version as of writing this (2.25.0). As a result, the stacktrace is entirely gone and logging appears to be behaving normally.

By doing this we also prevent discouraging novice contributors from contributing by falsely getting them to believe that they have performed something wrong during setup.

author: jackluo923
body:
**What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)**
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug Fix
- [ ] Optimization
- [ ] Documentation Update

<!-- Describe what has changed in this PR -->
This PR completes the end-to-end workflow for basic unstructured Ray log collection and uploading to Minio, utilizing the same CLP streaming compression and S3-compatible object storage upload approach employed at Uber. The system is currently set up to deliver near real-time log access via the browser-based log viewer. This workflow also establishes a foundation for future optimizations and feature enhancements.

<!-- Tell your future self why have you made these changes -->
**Why?**
Log management is especially challenging when logs must remain human-readable and be archived for future use, particularly in environments where users have limited access or control. Uber has an internal system that meets these requirements, offers a strong user experience, integrates seamlessly with existing infrastructure, and requires minimal maintenance. This PR seeks to open-source such system along with Michelangelo project. 

<!-- How have you verified this change? Tested locally? Added a unit test? Checked in staging env? -->
**How did you test it?**
A simple client-server execution model for a Michelangelo Ray job was evaluated. The detailed steps are outlined below, followed by a final screenshot of the log viewer displaying the log file.
1. Create k3d sandbox environment: `poetry run ma sandbox create`
2. Build example docker image for the standard environment : `docker build -t examples:latest -f ./examples/Dockerfile .`
3. Import built docker image into k3d cluster: `k3d image import examples:latest -c michelangelo-sandbox`
4. Execute a sample job: `PYTHONPATH="." poetry run python ./examples/nomic_ai/nomic_ai.py remote-run --image docker.io/library/examples:latest --storage-url s3://default --yes`
5. Navigate to MinIO's `logs` bucket to observe the generated log files
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4932f96-b304-4687-93b5-2cac92817e4e)
6. Navigate to the log file in the log-viewer: 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8895666-c4c5-4dfd-b8d9-d29a5b0a876d)

The temporal execution flow has also been tested with log collection, compression and upload flow.

<!-- Assuming the worst case, what can be broken when deploying this change to production? -->
**Potential risks**
In the worst-case scenario, systemic failures like a MinIO outage can completely disrupt log collection, storage, and viewing. For example, if MinIO object storage becomes unavailable, log uploads will be retried but may ultimately fail, leading to data loss and making log files inaccessible. However, since the log collection, storage, and viewing process operates independently from job execution, such an outage of the log collection, storage and viewing subsystem, it would not impact the execution of jobs themselves.

<!-- Is it notable for release? e.g. schema updates, configuration or data migration required? If so, please mention it, and also update CHANGELOG.md -->
**Release notes**
Add basic log collection, compression and upload flow for client-server execution model.

<!-- Does this PR introduce a user-facing or API change? Is user document updated? Is the change backward compatible? If so please update in wiki https://github.com/michelangelo-ai/michelangelo/wiki? -->
**Documentation Changes**
No user-facing or API change.

author: sdbondi
body:
Description
---
Implements versioned types on the storage layer for these types:
- substates
- transactions
- transaction executions
- proposal and timeout certificates
- epoch checkpoints

Adds a new unit test

Motivation and Context
---
This allows backward-compatible changes to data structures, which are "lazily" upgraded as they are loaded.
By lazy, we mean that if there is a schema update, we do not iterate through every record on startup / implement global migrations. Since there could be millions of entries, we instead encode the version at which the object was saved, and if/when it is loaded later, we convert it _infallibly_ to the latest schema. 

A unit test was implemented that shows that bincode decodes a type that has had new variants added after encoding.

author: robmry
body:
**- What I did**

- split out of https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/50140

Currently, when libnetwork selects gateway endpoints for a container (following an endpoint join/leave) it has to do a lot of work to decide whether old gateway configuration needs to be updated ... the new and old gateway endpoints may have different network drivers, gateway endpoints for IPv4/IPv6 need not be the same - and it's made particularly complicated by drivers being able to proxy from IPv6 host addresses to IPv4 container addresses. For example, when a container only has an IPv4 endpoint, proxying needs to be set up, then when an IPv6 endpoint is added, that proxying needs to be removed even if the IPv4 gateway hasn't changed.

Rather than trying to manage all that in libnetwork - just tell the driver whether its endpoint is currently acting as a gateway, and let the driver work out whether anything changed and what it needs to do about it.

With these changes - libnet is still tracking the gateway-ness itself, the simplifications are to-follow. But, libnet no longer needs to tell the driver whether it needs to proxy from IPv6-to-IPv4, the driver can work that out for itself based on whether there's an IPv6 gateway / whether it's the same as the IPv4 gateway.

See individual commits - libnet driver API change, remote-driver change, bridge-driver change.

body:
Boost tokenizer requires explicit "." after "$" to correctly extract JSON path tokens. Without this, expressions like "$[0].key" cannot be properly split, causing issues in downstream logic. This commit ensures a "." is automatically added after "$" to maintain consistent token parsing behavior.

### What problem does this PR solve?

```sql
SELECT JSON_EXTRACT('[{"key": [123]}]', '$[0].key');
```
before:
```
+----------------------------------------------+
| JSON_EXTRACT('[{"key": [123]}]', '$[0].key') |
+----------------------------------------------+
| NULL                                         |
+----------------------------------------------+
```
after:
```
+----------------------------------------------+
| JSON_EXTRACT('[{"key": [123]}]', '$[0].key') |
+----------------------------------------------+
| [123]                                        |
+----------------------------------------------+
```

author: tbavelier
body:
### What does this PR do?

* Ensures stable order when generating rules for non-deterministic CCRs (orchestrator explorer and annotationsAndLabelsAsTags)

### Motivation

* Frequent un-necessary updates for 2 CCRs: orchestrator and annotationsAndLabelsAsTags
* Root cause: non-deterministic generation of the `PolicyRule` slice within these `ClusterRoles`. The code iterated over maps to build the list of rules; because map iteration order is not guaranteed in Go, the resulting slice of rules could have a different order between reconciliations. This caused the deep equality check to fail, triggering an update even when the set of permissions was semantically identical.
* Solution: generate rules in a stable, deterministic order:
    * The approach involves a two-level sort in the functions that generate these rules:
        1. Sort resources within each API group: The list of resources (e.g., pods, services) for a given API group is sorted alphabetically.
        2. Sort the API groups themselves: The PolicyRule objects for each API group are then sorted alphabetically by the group name.

### Additional Notes

Anything else we should know when reviewing?

Are there minimum versions of the Datadog Agent and/or Cluster Agent required?

* Agent: vX.Y.Z
* Cluster Agent: vX.Y.Z

author: hook25
body:
## Description

Checkbox Remote is very, very slow when used over a slow connection. This is mostly due to a reason: When returning a mutable objects over an rpyc function, any further query on that object is a rpyc call. This is most evident in the following situations:
- Test plan selection (iterating over the testplan list takes ~600 (number of testplans) rpyc calls
- Test selection (modifying the desired list takes one call per test that will be selected, so deselecting just one test could lead to hundreds of rpyc calls)
- Calculating the return code of a test run (This iterated over the whole job_state_map, leading to ~10k rpyc calls as undesired jobs are present when no reboots are done)
- Exporting (Additional Configurations that were created client side lead to hundreds of rpyc remote calls when used afterward)

Additionally (this is a bit of a bonus), every test on a medium to high latency will always pay 0.5s to "wait" for the test to be completed + the latency. This adds a backoff mechanism that starts from 0 and goes to .5s

## Resolved issues

Fixes: https://warthogs.atlassian.net/browse/CHECKBOX-1956
Fixes: https://warthogs.atlassian.net/browse/CHECKBOX-1955

## Documentation

Documented this in the class docstring

## Tests

Added unit tests for /most/ of the api changed.

To try this change and simulate this issue locally modify `checkbox-ng/plainbox/vendor/rpyc/core/protocol.py` add to the serve function of the Connection class the following
```python
    def serve(self, timeout=1, wait_for_lock=True):  # serving
        import time
        time.sleep(.1)
```

This will simulate a 100ms latency (less than what it is Europe to Taiwan). Add the following test units to the metabox provider:
```
id: tons_of_jobs
_summary: Generates a lot of ids to fill the job_state_map
plugin: resource
shell: python
command:
  for i in range(100):
    print(f"id: stress_{i}")
    print()

unit: template
template-resource: tons_of_jobs
template-unit: job
id: {id}
template-id: template_tons_of_jobs
command:
  echo "Test {id}"
_summary: Test that stresses rpyc calls
flags: simple

unit: test plan
id: stress_remote_tps
_name: Stress test of the checkbox remote-api
bootstrap_include:
  tons_of_jobs
include:
  template_tons_of_jobs
```

A test run at 100ms latency of this testplan takes about 35minutes on main, 5m on this branch

Additionally, I've used this very ugly decorator to log all the calls made to the server to be able to track them down
```python
if os.getuid() == 0:
    log = open("/tmp/root_agent.log", "w+")
else:
    log = open("/tmp/usr_control.log", "w+")


def _log_call(f):

    # return f

    def _f(self, *args, **kwargs):
        global total
        total += 1
        import json

        log.write(json.dumps([str(x) for x in [total, *args, kwargs]]))
        log.write("\n")
        print(total, *args, kwargs)
        to_r = f(self, *args, **kwargs)
        if (
            not any(isinstance(to_r, x) for x in [str, int, float, bool])
        ) and to_r is not None:
            # breakpoint()
            ...
        return to_r

    return _f
```
Decorate all _handle_[...] functions in the Connection class to use this.

This pull request introduces significant improvements to password handling across the application by replacing the previous hashing mechanism with `bcrypt`. It also adds new utility methods for secure password operations, updates related services to use these utilities, and includes comprehensive tests for the new functionality. Additionally, the package dependencies have been updated to include `bcrypt` and its types.

### Password Handling Improvements
* Introduced a new `PasswordUtils` utility class for secure password hashing and verification using `bcrypt`. It includes methods `hashPassword` and `verifyPassword` with a default salt round of 12 for enhanced security. (`apps/api/src/common/utils/password.utils.ts`, [apps/api/src/common/utils/password.utils.tsR1-R40](diffhunk://#diff-f7797c76140c2bd43dd99fefddcfe1f1b953a4c7edf4c71b31bc8f4519c99700R1-R40))
* Updated `AuthService` to use `PasswordUtils` for password verification (`validateUser`) and hashing (`updatePassword`, `signIn`, and other methods). This replaces the previous SHA-256-based hashing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7e9ac17d7e6417f73125395406cff59ad6eee28fab0bcca2993d72e2e439fae6L33-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e9ac17d7e6417f73125395406cff59ad6eee28fab0bcca2993d72e2e439fae6L266-R273) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7e9ac17d7e6417f73125395406cff59ad6eee28fab0bcca2993d72e2e439fae6L57-R64)
* Updated `UserService` to hash passwords during user creation and password updates using `PasswordUtils`. Removed the old `@BeforeInsert` password hashing logic from the `User` entity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-759d7f3aab1b3cdd8f0e40f95e31e97fe36786ae99ebef111fdd6398caabc7c9L25-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-759d7f3aab1b3cdd8f0e40f95e31e97fe36786ae99ebef111fdd6398caabc7c9L49-R70) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2d7e6c140674d0b1484f16eb6bfa69e63f5a69156eb684c633b7723bb6fece6fL54-L60)

### Dependency Updates
* Added `bcrypt` (v6.0.0) and `@types/bcrypt` (v5.0.2) as new dependencies in `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` for secure password operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c40985d6d91eed8ae85ec1c8e754a85984ee32e156a600d2b7a467423d7e338R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c40985d6d91eed8ae85ec1c8e754a85984ee32e156a600d2b7a467423d7e338R56) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR65-R67) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-32824c984905bb02bc7ffcef96a77addd1f1602cff71a11fbbfdd7f53ee026bbR126-R128)

### Testing Enhancements

This ensures the correctness and security of the new password handling logic. (`apps/api/test/password.utils.spec.ts`, [apps/api/test/password.utils.spec.tsR1-R63](diffhunk://#diff-c7de9d6542406ef6239b7d48f48930f98655eba0ced893afef684ade964016d0R1-R63))

### Code Cleanup
* Removed the old SHA-256-based password hashing logic from the `AuthService`, `VerificationService`, and `User` entity. This includes removing the `createHash` import and related code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7e9ac17d7e6417f73125395406cff59ad6eee28fab0bcca2993d72e2e439fae6L4-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c8ac001aae37a78b4b4c26bb4378b3f6c08a6d2ffbc463a0b45d5b77186cd279R11) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2d7e6c140674d0b1484f16eb6bfa69e63f5a69156eb684c633b7723bb6fece6fL7-L12)
